steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Grease cookie sheets.
Beat brown sugar and butter together in a large mixing bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy; add egg and mix well. Stir in mincemeat.
Sift together flour, salt, and baking soda together; stir into mincemeat mixture.
Drop by teaspoonfuls, about 2 inches apart, on prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden brown, about 7 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Mincemeat Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These fragrant mincemeat cookies are bursting with prepared mincemeat pie filling for an old-fashioned festive cookie full of flavor and spice.
raw_recipe.name: Mincemeat Cookies

review.reviewBody: These cookies were very easy to make. They turned out moist and light. The taste was great.And they were also very much like those my grandmother used to make. Perfect treat for a cool fall or winter day.

I used half butter and half shortening. I lowered the temperature to 375 and baked for 12 to 14 minutes. I also put on with a cookie scoop and slightly pressed down before baking. I used homemade canned venison mincemeat. Also added a touch of cinnamon. They are good and moist. I would make again with these adjustments.

i just made a batch, adding 1/2 tsp. each of cinnamon, cloves and allspice. i had to bake them at 400 degrees for 12 minutes as my test cookie burned on the bottom at 425 degrees. i don't even like mincemeat, but i love these cookies!
Granny Seussie

Followed the recipe as written except I didn't have any shortening. Used 1/2 cup butter and 1/2 canola oil. None Such mincemeat in the jar. My cookies look just like the ones in the recipe photo. Used an 1+1/2 inch cookie scoop and got 12 cookies on a 13 x 9 sheet and they didn't run together. Did not grease the sheet nor use parchment paper. I let cookies stand 3-4 min before removing them and they came off nicely. Got 54 (4+1/2 doz) 3 inch cookies. Only 2 of us and 16 hrs later, there are 30 cookies left. I'm sure I will make these cookies again and will frost some with brown sugar frosting.

First attempt at mincemeat cookies. I chose this recipe because it was the only one I saw that called for brown sugar. I altered the recipe just a bit. I used 1 2/3 cup mincemeat (half of the jar) + 1/3 cup of applebutter. Used 2 eggs rather than 1. Used lard for shortening. They turned out great. Very light and cakelike. This is my recipe from now on!

This is a soft spice cookie that doesn't spread much. With my 1-inch cookie scoop, my yield was more than twice the 3 dozen listed. I did add some spices, vanilla, and more than 2 cups of mincemeat in order to increase the flavor. I'm afraid my "sprinkle" of cloves turned out to be more of a pour, but the flavor boost was more than OK. Not too sweet so a good foil for many of the holiday cookies that use lots more sugar. I did use parchment paper.

Really good recipe, but really bland the first time I tried them. Second time, I added cinnamon and nutmeg. Today, I decided to mimic the spices in mincemeat. I added 1 tsp cinnamon, and 1/2 tsp each cloves, nutmeg, and ginger. Seemed to be just right. Thanks for the recipe!

Hubby loves these cookies. I tweaked a bit and used "fake" sugar and added a tablespoon of molasses (to make it like brown sugar). I also used the 1/2 tsp clove, cinnamon, and allspice as suggested in another review. I used half wheat flour and half white. Thanks for the recipe!

I used my own homemade Green Tomato Mincemeat which I can at the end of the growing season so there is plenty of flavor there. I also used parchment paper for easy baking sheet prep as well as an insulated baking sheet. Easy to follow and definitely a keeper. I've been looking for a good recipe for mincemeat cookies and this is one of the best I've found.

Great Recipe! Tweeked it a bit. I added 1/2 teaspoon each of cloves, cinnamin, and allspice. I also added walnuts and peacans. My family says they don't like mincemeat but they ate these because they taste alot like gingerbread cookies. They stay moist and cake like. Reduce heat to about 410 if possilbe.

I used 1 1/2 cup butter, 3/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, and added walnuts and pecans. They were delicious and my family loved them. And I cut back on the oven temperature to 415 degrees.
These are divine! My dough was pretty soft, so I chilled it for an hour before scooping out and baking the cookies. Will definitely make these again and again!
I modified it: half this recipe, half the mincemeat bar recipe on the None Such mincemeat bottle.
Followed the recipe, but would double the mincemeat. They didn't have much flavor. Otherwise they are tasty. I will rate again after I double the mincemeat!
Pillowy soft. Made just as directed. Used a jar of Robertson’s mincemeat filling.
Cookies spread alot, make small mounds

as written, a solid '4' because it would have been too bland for my taste, however they produce a nice soft cookie in texture. I added mace, cinnamon, allspice, and clove. everyone loved the texture of these because of the softness. Honestly with mincemeat being so expensive, they tasted a lot like any other soft molasses cookie for the most part, but they were good.

Read comments that it was bland so I added 1/4 Cup granulated sugar and 1/8 teaspoon salt and 2 teaspoons vanilla. STILL BLAND. Definitely doesn’t match my Gramma’s recipe’s flavor. It’s missing a spice. Will try ground gloves and cinnamon.

This is the exact recipe that has been passed down from my dad’s family, which has been used since the 1780s. These are great for sitting in a regular cookie jar because they stay moist. Very old recipe.
